These are priors, not estimates from data. No benchmark tables were provided, so I could not check any of the pairs against results. Most interaction effects like these are small or inconsistent across datasets, so N carries most of the mass. The few directional leans reflect general intuition: capacity increases help most where capacity is scarce, and high learning rates are more fragile at depth.
